headline: PlayStation Store removing Studio Canal movies from libraries in Europe
summary: Sony is removing purchased Studio Canal films from European PlayStation Stores due to an expired licensing deal. The content will be unavailable starting September 1.
details: Sony has informed customers in several European countries that purchased Studio Canal movies will be removed from their digital libraries. This action is due to the upcoming expiration of a licensing agreement between Sony and Studio Canal.

Affected customers, including those in the UK, France, Italy, and Spain, will lose access to these films on September 1, 2024. The notice does not mention any provisions for refunds for the removed content.

This situation serves as a stark reminder that digital purchases do not always equate to permanent ownership. Content can be revoked due to expired licenses or service shutdowns, leaving consumers without access to what they thought they owned.

While the removal date is still several months away, there's a possibility for a renewed licensing agreement, similar to a past situation where Discovery shows were initially slated for removal but remained available after a new deal was struck.

headline_marked: Apple seeks exception to buy RAM from blacklisted Chinese supplier
headline: Apple seeks exception to buy RAM from blacklisted Chinese supplier
summary: The tech giant is reportedly looking to secure an exception from the US government to source memory chips from CXMT, a company with ties to the Chinese military.
details: Apple is reportedly seeking an exception from the Trump administration to purchase RAM chips from CXMT. This move comes as the company faces skyrocketing prices for RAM and storage, which have already led to price increases across many of its products.

CXMT is a Chinese supplier that has been blacklisted by the Pentagon due to alleged ties to the People's Liberation Army. While legally Apple is not barred from buying chips from CXMT, doing so would carry significant reputational risks.

There is a possibility that CXMT could still face export controls for undermining US security. The company was previously considered for the Commerce Department's "Entity List" but was not added as the White House was engaged in trade negotiations with China.

Granting Apple permission to work with CXMT could face significant backlash. Republican chair of the House China committee, John Moolenaar, stated that partnering with a Chinese military company would be a "grave mistake" and would increase US dependence on China.

The decision on whether to grant Apple this exception remains unclear. Tim Cook has previously engaged in efforts to build bridges with the Trump administration, but such a move could prove controversial.
